title: Air India App Gets Split-View Layouts Tailored for Apple's iPhone Duo
excerpt: Air India says its app was ready for the iPhone Duo from day one, with split-view and dual-pane layouts for booking, My Trips, check-in, flight status and loyalty.
body:
• Air India has optimised its mobile app for Apple's iPhone Duo, with support available from day one of the device's launch, according to the airline via FoneArena.
  • The update uses responsive, split-view and dual-pane layouts across Home, Flight Booking, My Trips, Check-in, Flight Status and Loyalty Profile.
  • For travellers: on the larger inner display you can compare flight options side by side and see multiple trip cards together with View Trip, Boarding Pass, Select Seat and Add Baggage actions on the same screen, with fewer taps and less scrolling.
  • The app adapts to four configurations — outer and inner displays, each in portrait and landscape.

What Air India changed

Air India has optimised its mobile app for the iPhone Duo, adapting the interface to the foldable device's larger display from day one of its launch. According to FoneArena's report, the update covers the Home screen, Flight Booking, My Trips, Check-in, Flight Status and Loyalty Profile. Digit, which reported the same update, said it is designed to make better use of the phone's larger display and offer a smoother experience for travellers.

https://www.instagram.com/p/Dd9S1_0miad/

The change is about layout, not a new booking product. Responsive layouts adjust content to the screen in use, while split-view and dual-pane designs organise information across the available space so users can view more information at a glance, compare flight options and access travel details with fewer taps and less scrolling, FoneArena reported.

How the layouts work across the Duo

The app supports the iPhone Duo's outer and inner displays in both portrait and landscape orientations. FoneArena listed the four configurations illustrated in the update as outer display in portrait, inner display in portrait, inner display in landscape and outer display in landscape. Digit reported that the app automatically adjusts its layout based on the screen being used, so travellers do not have to move between as many pages to see the same details.

On the Home screen, destination cards and other app content are displayed across the expanded viewing area. In Flight Booking, FoneArena said improved content organisation and visibility make it easier to compare available flight options — the clearest practical gain for someone weighing fares or timings before they book.

What changes in My Trips and on travel day

The My Trips section displays upcoming and past journeys, with multiple trip cards visible side by side. FoneArena listed the actions shown alongside journey details as View Trip, Boarding Pass, Select Seat and Add Baggage. That arrangement presents travel information and the actions a passenger is most likely to need together, rather than on successive screens.

The optimisation also covers Check-in and Flight Status, according to both reports. Those are the two functions travellers typically open under time pressure at an airport, so having them adapted to both the compact outer display and the unfolded inner display matters more than the cosmetic change on the Home screen.

Loyalty profile on the wider screen

The Loyalty Profile section displays My Activities, Vouchers, What's New and Earn with Partners, arranged to accommodate the wider layout so more information appears within a single view, FoneArena reported. Digit reported the same set of sections in its account of the redesign.

Travel PR News, publishing Air India's announcement, added context that Apple introduced the iPhone Duo in September, with general availability beginning on 23 October 2026, and that the device pairs a smaller external display with a larger inner display. The Videshi has not independently verified those device specifications from Apple in this run, and readers choosing a handset should check Apple's own specifications rather than relying on the airline's app notes.

What this means for diaspora travellers

For Indian travellers abroad who book and manage Air India journeys on their phones, the practical test is narrow: if you use an iPhone Duo, booking comparisons, trip cards and boarding-pass actions should now be visible together on the unfolded screen instead of spread across multiple taps. If you use any other phone, nothing in these reports describes a change to your app experience — the update is specific to the Duo's outer and inner displays and its four orientations.

Air India said the optimised app experience was available from day one of the iPhone Duo's launch, FoneArena reported. Travellers on the device should update the app and check the My Trips and Flight Booking layouts on the inner display to see the split-view arrangement described above.
